Here we get these temperatures and was wondering if it is feasible to ride in these temperatures with full gear
Question: People who wear always your full gear, what are you wearing when the temperature is 35-40 c (95-104F)

Kevlar jeans, jacket with the lining out and all vents open and front zip down around the chest area so some air can get in, leather gloves, boots and helmet. Not much changes for me.

I do wear an old t-shirt underneath and keep whatever I am going to wear once off the bike in a backpack. Sweat isn't much a problem while moving, but once you stop at a set of lights or are moving slowly through traffic and the airflow stops it does get pretty swampy.

On hot days ( over 20C in my opinion ) I make sure the liner is out of my jacket, all the vents are open and that's it. Decent jacket + decent gloves means I don't get too hot at speed. If I'm stopped for any length of time, I doff my gear. If I'm gonna go some place full of shitty stop and go driving, I'll use the car.

It gets even hotter here in Las Vegas: A couple of years ago it was 52c (126f). What I wear is similar to what I wear in the winter. Scorpion SGS leather gloves (summer gloves), alpinestars T-GP Plus R Air (What a stupid long name) mesh jacket, kevlar jeans(currently Dainese something or other), and alpinestars boots (smx-2 I believe, they are a couple of years old). I also have a modular helmet that I flip up at stoplights.

In the winter I use A* apex drystar gloves if it's really cold, which is rare here. I also have a heated jacket liner and a warm Dainese leather jacket that I will use depending on the warmth.
I do. My gear turns into a wetsuit that keeps me cool instead of warm. I'll get a nice layer of sweat going, and my pants are hot, but keeping the engine heat off of me.

What I haven't seen mentioned yet is that on hot days, the color of your gear can make a noticeable difference in your comfort. In addition to standing out visually, light colored gear will reflect more of the radiant heat coming from the sun.
Ride faster. I get the fuck out of the city as quick as possible and ride as fast as I need to.

Short answer: Expensive shit. The Rukka arma core range is really good. It says that it regulates temperature and I must admit it's the first of its kind to actually mean it. I've not experienced what it's like with temps higher than 35C but I imagine not much worse.

Gloves that are designed smartly can be a great ventilation source. Mine are not the most waterproof but hey it's gloves, you can always bring another pair somehow.

Alternatively kevlar jeans and mesh gear - mesh is supposed to be the best ventilation. Another option is the Klim kit: Klim Adventure Rally 2013 Note that it's waterproof.

If you don't need waterproof gear you can find some really good stuff with much more airflow.

well, it doesn't rain than often here but I am not sure how effective the gear is when it has lots of ventilations. To be honest I would prefer to ride in a colder country. It's easier to get worm than getting cool
I always remind myself that sweaty is better than dead-y. Especially as the whine of the water-cooling system reminds me that even my bike is hot.

I wear a t-shirt and a bullet helmet with a hankerchief over my face if I am not going far (and half gloves). if I am going far, I will wear my face mask.

im not really a ATGATT person, but I do have ATG.
My gear, and a thick sheen of sweat and thinly veiled impatience to get back up to speed.
At a minimum I wear my jacket, gloves, and helmet. The added benefit to the jacket is the prevention of a farmer's tan.

Jeans. Leather jacket. Gloves. Icon 1000 elsinore boots. My "summer" helmet which fits a bit bigger than normal so I get some venting. I wear 3/4 helmets so no vents. I have a full face with vents but I can't see well enough out of it.
This is what I wear in South Florida year round: http://www.motoport.com/index.php?option=com_redshop&view=product&pid=15&cid=27& Pants as well. Expensive tho...

My one piece has strategic vent spots that help cool, but I still bake when stopped. I have a two piece mesh that is much (MUCH) cooler. Usually it's the one piece for short hops and the two piece for longer or multiple hops. Mainly because I can disrobe quicker out of the one piece once home. Long freeway trips get the one piece every time. I always use gauntlet style gloves and boots.

What did you guys think of Jurassic World?

Growing up, Jurassic Park was my favorite movie, and it still is consistently in my top three. I was extremely pleased with JW as the dominant sequel in the series (Jurassic Park, JW, the Lost World, and then JP3 in my rankings).

By the way, obviously spoilers ahead.

So, I love how they modernized the park and the movie without ruining it. They brought everything up to speed, had a functioning park, and showed how awesome it was in operation. I think some of the things they did were distasteful to Hammonds wishes, but time and money erodes everything. One thing I mean by that is the petting zoo thing: having trics with saddles for kids to ride and interacting with them in such a way at such a young age. These people made a mistake that Ian Malcolm pointed out in the first movie: they acted like they were in control, when they have no way to be.

Overall, the movie was fantastic. Saw it last night with friends in normal theater, and me and a friend are going back tonight for IMAX 3D. Also, Chris Pratt has cemented himself as a fantastic actor; he did an amazing job in the movie.

My same feelings.

I wish they used the Indominus' camouflage more though, I had my thoughts as to what the Carnotaurus from The Lost World novel would be like, but we didn't get to see the camo a lot. :(

But yeah, movie was a highly satisfying Jurassic Park film.
Overall I enjoyed a lot of the throwbacks to JP1. I want to see it again to make more of an opinion but one thing that sticks out that I didn't like was the stare down near the end.
I really love Jurassic World. It was fun, funny and beautiful to watch. I am looking forward to seeing what the sequels will bring, especially with the plot points brought up in the movie.
